title: Tensor comparison for arbitrary torsion local systems
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\bar s$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], let $\Pi=\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ with its profinite topology [def-galois-fibre-functor], and let $R$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $n>0$. Use the local systems and the geometric-stalk equivalence with discrete continuous $R$-linear $\Pi$-modules of [lem-per-torsion-local-system-monodromy]. Thus a local system is an $R_S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] whose underlying sheaf of sets is a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of sheaves represented by finite etale covers. For any two such local systems $L,M$, the ordinary tensor product $L\otimes_{R_S}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is again a local system. There is a natural $\Pi$-equivariant $R$-linear isomorphism
$$(L\otimes_{R_S}M)_{\bar s}\cong L_{\bar s}\otimes_R M_{\bar s},$$
where the module tensor is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the action on the right is $g(x\otimes y)=gx\otimes gy$. The inverse sends the tensor of germs of two sections to the germ of their tensor. No finite generation, finite underlying stalk, flatness, or common finite trivializing cover is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, 7.2.1-7.2.4, pp. 301-302: module-object/tensor consequence of the equivalence with the classifying topos and preservation of colimits and finite limits. Tensor is intrinsic to a ringed topos: literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), and Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor).

proof.text: Put $V=L_{\bar s}$ and $W=M_{\bar s}$. By the monodromy equivalence these are discrete continuous $R$-linear $\Pi$-modules. For any $v\in V$, the orbit map from compact $\Pi$ to discrete $V$ is continuous, so its image is finite: the inverse images of the singletons cover $\Pi$ and a finite subcover contains the image. The $R$-span of the union of the orbits of a finite set of elements is therefore a finitely generated $\Pi$-stable submodule. Such submodules form a small directed poset (the sum contains any two, and zero is included), and their union is $V$. The same holds for $W$. Write these systems as $(V_i)$ and $(W_j)$. This uses finite orbits, not finite underlying modules or finiteness of $R$.

source.place: XVII 7.2.3, p. 301; elementary finite-orbit and finite-span argument

proof.text: Use a quasi-inverse of the monodromy equivalence to obtain local systems $L_i,M_j$ and their maps to $L,M$ corresponding to the inclusions $V_i\subset V,W_j\subset W$. These maps are ambient monomorphisms because the equivalence preserves and reflects ambient exact sequences. The colimit clause identifies the ambient colimits $\varinjlim_iL_i=L$ and $\varinjlim_jM_j=M$: on stalk modules their universal cocones are precisely the unions in Step 1. Every $L_i$ and $M_j$ is locally constant of finite type by the final clause of the same monodromy statement.

source.place: XVII 7.2.3-7.2.4, pp. 301-302; module objects and ambient colimits

proof.text: Fix $(i,j)$. The additive monodromy equivalence identifies $L_i\oplus M_j$ with the finitely generated module $V_i\oplus W_j$. Its finite-generation clause gives a connected finite etale Galois cover $c:T\to S$ trivializing this direct sum. Its open subgroup acts trivially on each summand, so its pullback clause makes both $c^{-1}L_i$ and $c^{-1}M_j$ constant. This cover is chosen separately for this pair; the argument does not choose a single cover for $L$ and $M$.

source.place: XVII 7.2.3-7.2.4, pp. 301-302; finite-generation consequence of open element stabilizers

proof.text: The tensor of constant module sheaves with values $A,B$ is the constant sheaf with value $A\otimes_R B$: apply the sheafification-tensor comparison to the constant presheaves $R,A,B$. The constant-scalar inverse-image comparison identifies $c^{-1}R_S$ with $R_T$, so module pullback along $c$ is ordinary inverse image. The ringed-topos pullback-tensor comparison now identifies $c^{-1}(L_i\otimes_{R_S}M_j)$ with $c^{-1}L_i\otimes_{R_T}c^{-1}M_j$, which is constant by the preceding calculation. Finite-etale descent in the monodromy statement implies that $L_i\otimes_{R_S}M_j$ is a local system on $S$.

Apply the colimit-preservation clause for sheaf tensor to the two small directed systems from Step 2, obtaining $L\otimes_{R_S}M\cong\varinjlim_i\varinjlim_j(L_i\otimes_{R_S}M_j)$. The coefficient category here is ordinary $R$-modules with its ordinary tensor, and its sheaf tensor is sheafification of the objectwise $R$-tensor. It agrees with the tensor over $R_S$ by the sheafification-tensor comparison applied with the constant presheaf $R$. All terms of the displayed iterated colimit are local systems by Step 4; the ambient-colimit clause of the monodromy equivalence says that its colimit is a local system. This proves tensor closure for the original arbitrary stalks.

source.place: Tag 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), hence preservation of colimits; Tag 0GMW; ILO XVII 7.2.4, p. 302

proof.text: Apply the tensor clause of the etale stalk comparison to $L,M$ with coefficient ring $R$. Its sheafified objectwise $R$-tensor agrees with $L\otimes_{R_S}M$ by Tag 0GMW as in Step 5. This gives a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $b:V\otimes_R W\longrightarrow(L\otimes_{R_S}M)_{\bar s}$ normalized by $b(s_{\bar s}\otimes t_{\bar s})=(s\otimes t)_{\bar s}$. The isomorphism requested in the statement is $b^{-1}$; in particular its inverse has exactly the stated formula on germs.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), applied to a geometric point; the explicit geometric-stalk comparison of lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar

proof.text: Check equivariance first for the pair $(L_i,M_j)$ on the cover $c:T\to S$ of Step 3, with $G=\operatorname{Aut}_S(T)$; choose a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ over $\bar s$ and let $\theta:\Pi\to G$ be the homomorphism of clause (1) of [lem-per-galois-descent-monodromy-tensor]. Since $c^{-1}L_i$ and $c^{-1}M_j$ are constant, the descent equivalence gives $L_i\cong T_{c,R}(V')$ and $M_j\cong T_{c,R}(W')$ for $G$-modules $V',W'$. By clause (1), $\gamma_{V'}$ and $\gamma_{W'}$ identify the stalks, with $\Pi$ acting through $\theta$; composing with the stalk isomorphisms of $L_i,M_j$, which are equivariant by the monodromy equivalence, we may take $V'=V_i$, $W'=W_j$ with $\Pi$ acting through $\theta$. Clause (2) gives $L_i\otimes_{R_S}M_j\cong T_{c,R}(V_i\otimes_RW_j)$ with diagonal $G$-action, sending $v\otimes w$ of constant sections on $T$ to the constant section $v\otimes w$; by clause (1) its stalk is $\gamma_{V_i\otimes W_j}$-identified with $V_i\otimes_RW_j$, $g$ acting as $\theta(g)\otimes\theta(g)$. The germ at $\bar t$ of $v\otimes w$ is $b(\gamma_{V_i}(v)\otimes\gamma_{W_j}(w))$ by the pure-germ normalization of $b$ in Step 6 (sections over etale neighbourhoods of $\bar t$ in $T$ are sections over etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$). Hence $b=\gamma_{V_i\otimes W_j}\circ(\gamma_{V_i}^{-1}\otimes\gamma_{W_j}^{-1})$ on pure tensors, so $g\,b(x\otimes y)=b(gx\otimes gy)$ for this pair. For arbitrary $x\in V,y\in W$, choose $i,j$ containing them. The map $L_i\otimes_{R_S}M_j\to L\otimes_{R_S}M$ is a map of local systems (Steps 4, 5), hence equivariant on stalks, and $b$ is natural; this gives the same equality for $L,M$. Pure tensors generate by the module-tensor definition, so the equality holds on all of $V\otimes_RW$. Finally the diagonal action is continuous: for a finite sum $\sum_kx_k\otimes y_k$, the intersection of the open stabilizers of all $x_k,y_k$ fixes the sum and is open. Naturality of $b^{-1}$ follows from that of $b$.

tool_uses.why: General sheafification-tensor comparison, needed for constant sheaves and the fixed-ring tensor convention; not supplied by the perverse unit.
General inverse image of constant scalar rings, needed to apply ringed-topos tensor pullback to the etale cover.
General tensor pullback along a ringed-topos morphism; used only for the finite cover, not as an alternative perverse route.
General tensor colimit preservation for ordinary module sheaves, needed to pass from finite-type pieces to arbitrary stalks.
General ordinary etale stalk-tensor comparison with its pure-germ normalization; no finite-type hypothesis.
